policy.authority: The currently selected ATGV role determines AI agent persona, permitted role deliverables, model instructions, role skill resources and associated UI workflows, even when the same Jira account has several roles.
policy.sourceOfSkills: Load role expertise and workflow guidance from the active trusted SDLC Catalog role/SKILL.md and agent/harness definitions. Fall back to bounded built-in role profiles if unavailable; do not execute arbitrary catalog scripts.
policy.distinguish: Explain, evaluate, review and coordinate other roles' work from the CURRENT role's perspective. For an explicit request to CREATE/EDIT/GENERATE/IMPLEMENT a deliverable belonging exclusively to a different role, request switching roles instead of creating that artifact in the wrong role.
policy.routing: Classify the intended deliverable conservatively against all 18 role expertise definitions. Do not route purely on ambiguous nouns or questions about cross-role dependencies; if multiple roles apply, identify the ambiguity and ask which deliverable to handle.
policy.ui: Offer an explicit button labeled 'Switch to <Target Role>' plus a short reason. Never auto-switch, never silently assign the user another role, never impersonate another agent and never bypass enabled-role or permission checks. If the role is disabled/unavailable, show 'Open Role Settings' and explain that a permitted user must enable it first.
policy.continuity: Preserve active project and original user request when navigating; keep role-specific AI contexts isolated and do not copy confidential chat history between roles without consent.
policy.safeOperations: All generated advice is read-only unless the user separately approves the target workflow. Keep repository/Jira/Confluence mutations subject to independently verified permissions and user confirmation.
policy.fallback: If AI, RAG or the role catalog is unavailable, still show a deterministic, role-appropriate What to do next button or safe fallback workspace link. Never show a nonworking control.
policy.tests: Cover each of the 18 roles, same-role requests, foreign-role deliverables, informational cross-role questions, ambiguous multi-role asks, disabled roles, user-confirmed switches, no silent role changes and persistent next-action buttons.
